sources.text: Rockstar Games have released 38 new screenshots of Grand Theft Auto 6 , ahead of its release later this month. These screenshots, found on a dedicated launch gallery website Rockstar has created , prompts viewers to scroll down and take in the sights of several high quality in-game screenshots snapshotting all kinds of people, places, and events. These include, but are not limited to, a DJ set in-action, a man and his pitbull looking tough to the camera, a tattooed man getting his hair done (machine gun on hand), and a daring motorbike escape. However, my personal favourite has got to be a lively shot of a dive bar. A band - seemingly called The Rusty Anchor is playing - and some older ladies appear to be having a friendly chat with an open-shirt-wearing geezer enjoying a beer. You can find all the new images in an image gallery below. So look through them at your pleasure: Grand Theft Auto 6 is due to release on the 19th November on PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. A few days prior, Rockstar employees are voting on whether or not they'd like to officially recognise a developer union , as the Rockstar vs IWBG union employment tribunal comes to a close on the eve of GTA 6's release date.

sources.title: Is Kodak Black in GTA 6? Rapper’s Grand Theft Auto Cameo, Explained
sources.text: Recently, Rockstar Games released another slew of Grand Theft Auto 6 screenshots, dubbed a ‘launch gallery’, and revealed a few unknown details about the game. From the identity of Jason Duval’s military pup to the identity of a celebrity cameo, we had a few tidbits surface in these remarkable screenshots. That celebrity cameo arrived in the form of Kodak Black, a rapper and singer from Florida. This has opened up speculation that more celebrity cameos will land in Grand Theft Auto 6, but there’s a pretty big twist here. Kodak Black is in Grand Theft Auto 6, and it looks like he’s playing himself . It’s no big secret that Rockstar Games often brings in well-known celebrities to play Grand Theft Auto characters, and there’s already a slew of big names confirmed for the game’s radio stations , but this is the first character we’ve seen modelled on a celebrity. But this character isn’t just modelled on Kodak Black. It appears to be Kodak Black. It was noticed that everything about this character, including the tattoos, is a perfect replication of the real-world rapper. This is huge, because Rockstar Games doesn’t do that . If a celebrity has a role in Grand Theft Auto, they’re often playing a satirized character or something similar, and they never assume their own real-world identity. GTA is the ultimate societal parody, but Kodak Black being a character could indicate more celebrity presences surfacing. And that has prompted many to wonder who else from the state of Florida could appear in GTA 6. For those not in the know, Kodak Black, real name Bill Kahan Kapri, is an American hip-hop and rap artist, most notable for ‘ No Flockin ‘, a track he released more than a decade ago. He’s a prolific artist who has built a reputation for being a guy in the know, well connected to other artists. Earlier this year, he lived a bit of the Grand Theft Auto life when he was arrested in Florida on an MDMA trafficking charge, and previously, he served time in prison. Do you hope we see more celebrity appearances in Grand Theft Auto 6? Let us know your thoughts on the Insider Gaming Discord server . You'll probably find him playing a post-apocalyptic game or an extraction shooter somewhere.

sources.title: Bethesda Is Already Selling The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel Merch
sources.text: Hot on the heels of Bethesda Game Studios officially announcing the full name of its highly anticipated next project, The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, the developer has already put up merch for the upcoming RPG on its online shop. You can be the first person in your friend group with a Sentinel-logo hoodie or T-shirt. And like the Ford Model T, it comes in any color you want, as long as it's black. The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel hoodie is $64.99, while the identical item in T-shirt form is $34.99. Hat tip to @MrMattyPlays on X for first spotting the Sentinel merch. Bethesda says, "Celebrate The Elder Scrolls VI. Your next journey through Tamriel will be in The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. Show off your excitement with the official hoodie!" And if you're interesteed in ordering, note the disclaimer: "This hoodie runs small. For the perfect fit, we recommend ordering one size larger than your usual size." The T-shirt shares an identical description, minus the note about it running small. You'll have plenty of time to break in either of these clothing items, as Sentinel isn't expected to be released for at least a couple more years . That would mean it might be at least a decade between the original announcement of The Elder Scrolls 6 and the time it's finally on your hard drive. Regardless, it's arguably the biggest game Xbox has in its portfolio by a country mile and when the release date finally arrives, it's going to be a very, very big deal. Amidst all of the changes at Xbox this year, it will be interesting to see if, a) The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel will be available on Xbox Game Pass Ultimate on day one, b) if it might line up with the launch of Xbox's next-gen Project Helix console/gaming PC hybrid , and/or c) if it ends up being an Xbox console exclusive . Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

sources.title: Skyrim Game Director Has a Very Specific Wishlist For The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel
sources.text: The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel is probably still a couple years away , and we don't know much about Bethesda's next big MMO. However, the game director for Skyrim has come out with a couple of specific requests for the game. Former Bethesda design director Bruce Nesmith sat down on The Examined Game podcast to talk about his time at the company. But, about 40 minutes into the interview, the YouTuber asked Nesmith about what he'd like to see from The Elder Scrolls VI, and there are two things, better mounts and better ladders. And that latter one is how you can tell that he's a game director. Wanting better mounts in Elder Scrolls is almost universal for fans, as Skyrim doesn't exactly have a great mount system. As Nesmith describes the problem, "you can ride a horse, but that's all you can do in Skyrim. Thats it. You just ride the horse. Well, I should be able to do other things with the horse, too, like maybe fight on the horse, or have it fight with me, or you know, stuff like that." To be clear, Nesmith now spends his days writing novels, and doesn't have anything to do with Sentinel, but it would be cool to be able to have some kind of mounted combat system in The Elder Scrolls VI. For instance, I've been getting back into Monster Hunter Wilds ahead of the expansion, and the way you can use your Seikret to dodge out of boss mechanics and manage your inventory while avoiding attacks is huge, and would be great in other RPGs. But as for ladders, Nesmith request seems odd until he starts to explain the way that ladders limited game design in Skyrim. As he explains, "you don't climb up and down ladders. It seems simple, it seems stupid, but you don't climb up and down ladders, which really limits the art team in terms of how they can do multi-layer things. You know, all the ladders in Skyrim, you click on the ladder, and poof you're at the top. Or you have to climb a stair." Some of that is obviously the limited technology of 2011, but it's apparently something Bethesda tried to solve, before giving up to prioritize other elements of the massive RPG. When Nesmith tried to get ladders solved in Skyrim, he says "to do ladders, you have to deal with a whole host of questions that our programmers very legitimately put in front of us and said, 'you give me answers to these, I'll tell you how much programming time it's going to take to make them.' and that caused problems right there." Even when I sit down and think about it, I can't really think of any game that really nails ladders, and a lot of games have problems with them in one way or another, especially around the era of Skyrim. Nesmith goes on to explain a lot of the specific problems that enemy AI has with ladders, like its ability to decide whether or not to wait for you at the top, or to climb back down the ladder to come after you. These problems have all been solved in one way or another in other games, but I'd hope that Skyrim finds a way to solve the issue as well. Either way, The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel is still a few years away, even though Bethesda is already selling merch . We'll have to wait a bit to see more about the game, but there are some signs about what might be in the game, and that might even include ship combat – or at least I hope. Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

sources.title: Skyrim's lead designer has 2 big asks of The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, and only one of them is something most players have ever thought about
sources.text: The classic children's board game: horses and ladders. Psst, hey kid, what are the big changes you'd like to see in The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel ? Because all have them, don't we? We've all got our big lists for Todd Howard: Five Easy Ways to Turn This Enormously Profitable Ship Around. You know who else has some changes he'd like to see in Sentinel? Bethesda alum and Skyrim lead designer Bruce Nesmith, who recently sat down with The Examined Game and said that the things he'd really like Bethesda to knuckle down on in TES 6 are mounts and ladders. "I'd like to see a much better implementation of mounts," said Nesmith. "That's been a common complaint; I'm not alone in that." But mounts can be hard to get right. "They're really tricky, there's a lot of hard decisions to be made in those. "You can ride a horse, but that's all you can do in Skyrim. That's it, you just ride the horse. Well, I should be able to do some other things too, maybe fight on the horse, or have it fight with me, you know, stuff like that." In fairness, Skyrim does have some fairly rudimentary mounted combat—though players had to wait for it to be added in a patch back in the day—but I suspect Nesmith would like to see something a bit less awkward in future Elder Scrolls games. I imagine a lot of players would echo Nesmith on mounts. I'm less sure they share his concern about ladders, which strikes me as a very charming and very game-designer-y fixation to have. "You don't climb up and down ladders [in current Elder Scrolls games]. It seems simple, it seems stupid, but you don't climb up and down ladders!" But you know what? I'm on board. Not having proper ladders, says Nesmith, "really limits the art team in terms of how they can do multi-layer things. You know, all the ladders in Skyrim, you click on the ladder, poof you're at the top, or you have to climb a stair." Advanced ladder tech has its costs, though. "To do ladders, you have to deal with a whole host of questions, which our programmers very legitimately put in front of us, and said 'You gimme answers to these, I'll tell you how much programming time it's gonna take to make them'. And that caused problems, right there". Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. There are, it turns out, a whole lot of ladder questions that arise if you try to implement them in your game. If two people use a ladder at once, what happens? How do NPCs make strategic decisions about them? How do you create animations and behaviours for characters getting hit while climbing, or dying while climbing? All these things and more pile up, which is why Bethesda decided to spend its time on other stuff, historically. Now, of course, it's not Nesmith's problem, and the man wants his mounts and ladders. Bravely, as someone else who also does not have to design The Elder Scrolls 6, I say give them to him. One of Josh's first memories is of playing Quake 2 on the family computer when he was much too young to be doing that, and he's been irreparably game-brained ever since. His writing has been featured in Vice, Fanbyte, and the Financial Times. He'll play pretty much anything, and has written far too much on everything from visual novels to Assassin's Creed. His most profound loves are for CRPGs, immersive sims, and any game whose ambition outstrips its budget. He thinks you're all far too mean about Deus Ex: Invisible War. sources.title: Nintendo Exec Bill Trinen Explains Why the Ocarina of Time Remake Is the Perfect First The Legend of Zelda Game
sources.text: Nintendo of America Vice President of Player & Product Experience Bill Trinen has seen a lot of Zelda games in his nearly 30-year career at the company. He got his start translating bug reports on the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the N64 in the '90s. And with the newly released and critically acclaimed remake, he acknowledged that, internally, there's always a bit of a different buzz when working on a new Zelda game. "Zelda games always come kind of with their own unique energy," he told me at the launch event for the Ocarina of Time Remake at the Nintendo Store in San Francisco. "This moment in particular, I think, is big for all of them [internally], both just because, like, we've talked about how much the game meant to a lot of people back then, but also the role that it plays within the overall Zelda 40th anniversary." The original Legend of Zelda was released for the NES in 1986. Ocarina of Time, in 1998, was the first 3D Zelda game, something that Trinen said this remake release brings back memories of. "The [1998] game itself was just so foundational for [this] kind of 3D adventure game, as a whole, and it just was this moment in time where it was like, everybody was on this journey together." Ocarina of Time has stood the test of time in being regarded as one of the greatest games of all time, but not everyone has played it , whether it was because they didn't have an N64 back then, or that they weren't born yet. Trinen has a message for those players: "This is the perfect place for your first Zelda game, because you are gonna learn everything that there is about the world and the characters that will serve sort of as the foundation for all the others, all the games that came after," he said. "This game is sort of a really foundational story for the lore of the Legend of Zelda. It really tells the story of Link and his journey becoming a hero. It tells the story of Link and his connection to Zelda and their relationship with Ganondorf. And overall, it communicates kind of what is at the moral core of is all the series, which is the idea that wisdom and courage combined can overcome power." Trinen also shared his favorite moment from Ocarina of Time [SPOILER WARNING] . "I have to say my favorite moment in Ocarina is the moment when Link leaves Kokiri Forest for the first time. It's an emotional moment. You say goodbye to a friend. There's a tinge of sadness to it, and then the whole world opens up before you, and you just see Hyrule Fields spread out. And all the possibility and exploration and discovery that awaits, you just sort of see across the field in the list, and you start to wonder, 'Okay, what am I gonna do next?' So it's sort of this really magical moment of almost, you know, leaving your childhood for the first time and setting out into the world, that happens early in the game, and it's a really special part of Link's overall journey." Finally, when I put Trinen on the spot to ask him his favorite Zelda game of all time, he said it's changed over time and answered with a big smile on his face. "Oh, you know, it changes with time. You know, there were points where it was Majora's Mask, and points where it was Wind Waker, or Breath of the Wild. I would say, the role that Ocarina of Time played both in terms of the impact on Nintendo, the impact on the games industry, the impact it had for the series overall, that makes it such a core experience that the Nintendo Switch 2 version is my current new favorite." The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is out now exclusively on the Nintendo Switch 2. You can read our review of the game here , or check out our look at the Biggest Changes from the original 1998 game. sources.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake reportedly running at 60 fps on PC just hours after game's official Nintendo Switch 2 release
sources.text: Visual and performance issues not quite ironed out yet, which will be music to Nintendo's ears. I've spent all night playing The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on the Switch 2, and it's a fantastic experience, but some would prefer to tinker and toil over an emulator than enjoy Link's new look. The game is already running on PC, but performance issues are aplenty. You can see progress is moving pretty fast from the emulator crowd, just from these two videos by Unreal Gaming PC on YouTube. Published on the game's official launch day, November 5, this video shows the game getting over the splash screen and running the cutscenes fairly well; however, it suffers from bad flickering, stuttering, and frame rates around the 20-30 fps mark during gameplay. 12 hours later, another video. This time showing the game running between 30–60 fps during gameplay, albeit with some persistent flickering and stutters throughout. There's undoubtedly still a long way to go to a playable experience to match the native Switch 2, but that's marked progress for half a day's work. Especially considering the game is designed for an Arm-powered handheld with very different hardware to what's running the emulator ( Ryzen 7 9800X3D , 64 GB of RAM, and RTX 4080). User akakevinvro on X also posted a video claiming a pretty steady 60 fps. Both are running on the Lichii emulator for the Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2. It's called the "VERY experimental Nintendo Switch 2 emulator" on its GitHub page. It's an open-source project that has similarities to projects of the same ilk, such as Yuzu. Yuzu's developers settled a legal dispute with Nintendo of America and shut down development of the emulator in 2024 . Nintendo has a long history of taking down projects it deems to infringe on its rights, while emulators such as the now defunct suyu often argue that they do not circumvent Nintendo's privacy measures. sources.title: Nintendo says it isn't planning any more Switch 2 price hikes
sources.text: Nintendo, which unveiled the results of the first half of its fiscal year 2027 earlier today , has now said it has access to enough quantities of memory to manufacture more Switch 2 consoles. As a result, the platform holder does not plan to increase the price of the Switch 2. That's according to Reuters , citing Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa. Nintendo, which has so far sold 26m Switch 2 consoles, has already raised the price of the console earlier this year. The price hikes, which took effect on 1st September in the US, Canada, Japan and Europe, saw the console's price increase by $50 / €30 / ¥10,000. Although that was technically the first price hike for the console itself, prior to the Switch 2's launch last year, Nintendo raised the price of Switch 2 accessories in the US as a result of the Trump Administration's tariffs. The reason that would cause Nintendo to raise prices again is the same that already caused rival PlayStation and Xbox to do so: AI-driven, global memory and storage shortages . PlayStation already raised PS5 and PS5 Pro prices , on several occasions . Xbox has likewise gone through multiple rounds of price hikes for its Series X and Series S consoles , with the most recent having taken place in August . That same crisis pushed one of Nintendo's longtime ROM suppliers to exit the business , opting instead to focus on the more lucrative business segments. ROM memory is used in Switch cartridges, though Nintendo hasn't commented on the news. Incidentally, Switch 2 hardware sales have been in decline for several quarters now compared to its banner launch in 2025. Still, Switch 2 sales are tracking ahead of the Switch 1.

sources.title: Nintendo says it’s not planning another Switch 2 price hike
sources.text: Nintendo’s president says it will have ‘sufficient’ RAM as shortages drive up console prices.﻿ Nintendo’s president says it will have ‘sufficient’ RAM as shortages drive up console prices.﻿ Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa said during the company’s latest earnings call that it’s “not considering additional changes” to the Switch 2’s price, Reuters reports. The Switch 2 got a $50 price hike earlier this year, bringing its starting price up to $499. Nintendo said in Thursday’s earnings report that Switch 2 sales have dropped 37.4 percent year-over-year. According to Reuters , Furukawa also gave an update on the RAM shortage, saying, “There has been no major change to the memory situation and Nintendo is in a position to secure sufficient quantities.” Earlier this week, one of Nintendo’s Switch 2 cartridge suppliers announced it plans to stop making ROM memory to focus on memory for data centers instead. Demand from AI data centers is driving the ongoing RAM shortages that’s leading to a wave of tech price increases. Microsoft has raised Xbox Series X / S prices multiple times now, increasing the Series S’s starting price from $299 to $499. The PS5 has also been hit with price hikes, taking its starting price up to $649 .

sources.title: Nier: Automata is now a 366GB install on Steam after a small update, up from 50GB
sources.text: Square Enix still recommends 50GB to install the action RPG on Valve's store Nier: Automata has received a small update on PC which adds three new language options to the storied action RPG, and somehow it has apparently increased its install size from 50GB to a staggering 366GB. After seeing chatter online, we confirmed this ourselves. When we tried to reinstall Nier: Automata through Steam, we were told we need 366.56GB of space. I don't know what happened – what wasn't compressed, what was duplicated, what accidentally got folded in – but Square Enix or Platinum Games have septupled Nier: Automata's hard drive demand. Users speculate that the entire game was mistakenly stapled to the DLC footprints, so duplication might be the most accurate. Hilariously, the patch notes for the update seemingly responsible could fit on your thumb. "The Steam patch released on November 6th, 2026 includes the following," the update reads. Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and Korean are now supported. Notably absent from these patch notes is anything to the tune of: Also, heads up folks, 600% more content or assets. Outside of welcome language support, the game is unchanged according to all early analysis. In the Steam discussion for this update, other users have reported a chunky but sensible 8GB download for the patch itself. The storage recommendation on the Steam store page system requirements is also the same: "50 GB available space." It doesn't look like a nefarious situation, so what the heck happened? What have they been feeding these androids? Were we trying to one-up Phantom Blade Zero's 300GB pre-load ? Is director Yoko Taro personally behind this, or is he as confused as we are? It's got to be one of the two. That is a man with two modes : uncontainable chaos and unshakable aloofness. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more I haven't seen any official accounts address this file size explosion online, and I truly cannot wait to read the explanation. For Nier Automata, Yoko Taro just made the RPG he wanted to and "tried to stay hidden from Square Enix as much as possible" Austin has been a game journalist for 12 years, having freelanced for the likes of PC Gamer, Eurogamer, IGN, Sports Illustrated, and more while finishing his journalism degree. He's been with GamesRadar+ since 2019. They've yet to realize his position is a cover for his career-spanning Destiny column, and he's kept the ruse going with a lot of news and the occasional feature, all while playing as many roguelikes as possible. sources.title: NieR: Automata Devs Address 366 GB Update
sources.text: An update for NieR: Automata has released, accidentally requiring 366 GB of space. The base game only requires 50 GB of space to download. The update is meant to add simplified Chinese, traditional Chinese, and Korean languages to the game, according to their November 5 update note on Steam . On the NieR Series X page (formerly Twitter), there is a note from the developers apologizing for the error and noting that they are working on a resolution. They also shared a workaround until it is fixed. Instead of downloading the giant update, selecting the “Properties” menu, then “DLC” and unselecting the DLC items allows players to keep playing the base game for now. Although a DLC for the game hasn’t been released since 2024, there is still a large player base. In February of 2026, the game celebrated having surpassed 10 million copies shipped and sold . What is the largest game download you’ve had to do? Let us know your thoughts via the free Insider Gaming Discord server . stories.title: Analysis: one in three acquired game studios has been shut down since 2000
stories.summary: A new analysis of over 300 game studios acquired by big companies since 2000 shows one in three studios has since been shut down completely, half of which were shuttered within five years of the acquisition. Read more

sources.name: GamesIndustry.biz
sources.title: Analysis: one in three acquired game studios has been shut down since 2000
sources.text: Who buys a studio is the best predictor of its fate, according to the analysis A new analysis of over 300 game studios acquired by big companies since 2000 shows one in three studios has since been shut down completely, half of which were shuttered within five years of the acquisition. Sebastian Cardoso, who has previously worked at Riot, Crytek, and EA, spent about three months tracking 303 PC and console studios acquired over the last 25 years. He published the results on his Game Studio Unlocked newsletter this week, alongside the full dataset. According to his findings, 60.8% of acquired studios either saw their games decline or were shut down altogether, and just one in four acquired studios "came through both producing at or above their old level, as well as institutionally whole." The biggest factor, he found, was who bought the studio. All 17 of Activision Blizzard's ownership periods ended in decline or closure, as did every one of Disney's, Midway's, and Thunderful's. EA's figure was 83%. Of the 283 developers in the census, just 71 studios, or 25.1%, were still making games as well as before and hadn't been hit by mass layoffs, absorbed into their parent or lost their leadership, although some of that is down to Cardoso's own rules. He counts a studio as having declined if it was absorbed into its owner or moved onto support work, even if its games held up. Take those cases out and the 60.8% figure drops to 51.6%. Nintendo hasn't lost a single studio. It has bought six in 24 years and closed none, and Kadokawa, Krafton, and Sumo Group also have clean records. By comparison, 63% of Microsoft's ownership periods ended in decline or closure, as did 58% of Sony's, 50% of Tencent's, and 43% of Embracer's. Cardoso puts the difference down to whether a company buys studios to "feed a machine" or because it "wanted to own good studios." Closures have also accelerated. Only one acquired studio in the census shut down between 2019 and 2022, but 33 have shuttered since 2023. Cardoso also tracked 50 notable independent studios over the seven years from October 2019 to October 2026. Just 2% of them closed, against 12.6% of acquired studios, though he points out the independent figure rests on a single closure. Studios that big companies founded themselves did even worse as, of 56 in the census, 87.5% declined or were shut, and 18 of the 34 that closed never released a game. NetEase alone opened eight studios between 2020 and 2023 and all eight have since been closed.

sources.name: Insider Gaming
sources.title: One-Third of Acquired Game Studios Have Shut Down Since 2000
sources.text: A new report found that a third of studios acquired by larger companies since 2000 have shut down. Layoffs and closures have become uncomfortably frequent nowadays; sometimes it’s almost every month that you hear about some kind of layoffs and studio closures. The biggest one in recent times was BioWare , but there have been so many gems that have been lost over the years, mostly recently. A report from Sebastian Cordoso (via TechSpot ) reveals that a third of all acquired studios since 2000 have been shut down. The investigation spans over 362 studios that have been acquired since 2000, and close to 60% of them have declined or shut down. The data reveals that only 12.4% (45 studios) have thrived, 27.3% (99 studios) are stable, 26.2% (95 studios) have declined, and 34% (123 studios) have shuttered. More Insider Gaming: Mass Effect’s Petition Has More Traction Than The ‘Save Physical Games’ Petition The report also breaks down the studios shut down by company, with Activision Blizzard topping the charts by shutting down all 17 acquired studios. Thunderful and Disney follow, and at the other end of the list are studios like Nintendo, Krafton, and Kadokawa that haven’t shut down any of the studios they have acquired. Other companies such as Microsoft have shut down 63% of acquired studios; Ubisoft has closed 62%, Take-Two and Epic Games are at 60%, and Sony is at 58%. Interestingly, only two acquired studios in the census have been closed between 2019 and 2022, and there have been 71 studio closures in the past 46 months. What are your thoughts on one-third of all acquired studios since 2000 shutting down? Leave your thoughts down in the comments, and join the official Insider Gaming Discord server . stories.title: Assassin’s Creed Valhalla: a atualização com novo jogo+, novo recurso e muito mais
stories.summary: The post Assassin’s Creed Valhalla: a atualização com novo jogo+, novo recurso e muito mais appeared first on Xbox Wire em Português .

sources.name: Xbox Wire BR
sources.title: Assassin’s Creed Valhalla: a atualização com novo jogo+, novo recurso e muito mais
sources.text: A atualização mais pedida de Assassin’s Creed Valhalla já está disponível no XBOX Series X|S e no XBOX One. A atualização traz diversas novidades empolgantes ao jogo, oferecendo novas maneiras de aproveitar sua aventura viking. O grande destaque é a chegada do Novo Jogo+, um dos recursos mais pedidos pelos fãs de Assassin’s Creed Valhalla . As demais novidades do patch garantem que sua experiência após o fim da campanha e no Novo Jogo+ seja renovada e desafiadora, com recompensas que fazem tudo valer a pena. Confira o que esperar da atualização mais pedida: Conversamos com o designer-chefe de jogo, David Larouche, para saber mais sobre a atualização e como a equipe coloca os jogadores no centro de tudo o que faz. Quais novidades desta atualização são uma resposta direta aos comentários da comunidade? David Larouche : o Novo Jogo+ foi, sem dúvida, o recurso mais pedido pelos fãs. Assassin’s Creed Valhalla é um jogo imenso, mas, para algumas pessoas, jogar uma vez só não basta. Com esta atualização, estamos muito empolgados em permitir que nossos vikings mais dedicados vivam essa aventura novamente, mas, desta vez, com o personagem que tinham ao final da campanha. Como a equipe garantiu que os recursos pedidos atendessem às expectativas dos jogadores? DL : queríamos que a experiência do Novo Jogo+ não fosse apenas jogar tudo de novo; queríamos permitir que os jogadores continuassem aumentando seu poder, percebessem uma progressão em etapas menores e seguissem aprimorando seus personagens. Por todos esses motivos, adicionamos um modo de progressão estendida, mais melhorias para todas as peças de equipamento divino, uma nova categoria de runas e mais de 300 novas opções de bônus de runas que podem ser gravados na Forja de Runas — e todos esses recursos também estão disponíveis fora do Novo Jogo+. Com todas essas novidades, acreditamos que a experiência do Novo Jogo+ incentivará os jogadores a explorar todo o potencial de Eivor. Houve algum desafio inesperado na implementação dessas novidades? DL : acho que o mais surpreendente para nós foi justamente não termos encontrado nenhum grande desafio que nos deixasse sem saber como avançar. Conseguimos reunir uma equipe muito competente de desenvolvedores com experiência em adicionar o Novo Jogo+ a jogos já existentes; o processo de produção foi incrivelmente tranquilo. Há algum recurso que você esteja especialmente empolgado para ver no jogo? DL : com a atualização, transformamos praticamente todos os bônus presentes em itens em runas que podem ser gravadas na Forja de Runas, independentemente de terem sido lançados na experiência estendida, em uma expansão ou até mesmo na Loja. Mal posso esperar para ver como os jogadores vão combinar todos esses bônus e criar os mais variados tipos de sinergia. Tenho certeza de que há muitas combinações poderosíssimas a serem descobertas! Assassin’s Creed Valhalla recebeu sua última atualização de conteúdo há anos. Por que lançar a atualização mais pedida para os jogadores agora? DL : Valhalla pode ter recebido sua última atualização de conteúdo há anos, mas isso não significa que os jogadores deixaram de se importar com o jogo — e nós também não. Sabemos que o Novo Jogo+ é algo que a comunidade deseja há muito tempo e, quando surgiu a oportunidade de finalmente torná-lo realidade, mal podíamos esperar para seguir em frente. No fim das contas, trata-se de dar aos jogadores de longa data mais um motivo para voltar a um mundo ao qual dedicaram tanto tempo e reviver a jornada de Eivor sob uma nova perspectiva, levando consigo boa parte do que conquistaram pelo caminho. O fato de algum tempo ter passado não torna essa experiência menos significativa para nós nem, esperamos, para nossos jogadores. Qual é a importância da comunidade de Assassin’s Creed para a equipe da franquia? DL : a comunidade é extremamente importante para mim e para a equipe. Pessoalmente, acompanho as redes sociais com frequência para ver sobre o que os jogadores estão conversando e, como equipe, prestamos muita atenção aos comentários e às conversas pela internet. Adoramos ver o que os jogadores criam e compartilham sobre nossos jogos. Essa conexão com a comunidade é incrivelmente gratificante e é uma das principais razões pelas quais fazemos o que fazemos. Jogue hoje mesmo Assassin’s Creed Valhalla com a atualização mais pedida no XBOX Series X|S e no XBOX One.

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: PlayStation sees record high player numbers and increased revenue for Q2 2026, and a lot of that success is down to Marvel's Wolverine
sources.text: As part of today's (Thursday 5th November, 2026) financial results, Sony has confirmed that monthly active users, referred to as MAU, across both PlayStation 4 and 5, reached 127 million in September. This represents a seven percent growth year-on-year for the company, and sets a new record high. In Layman's terms, this simply means that more people are engaged with the PlayStation ecosystem now than ever before. And it's not just that there are more people using machines and occasionally booting up their consoles; active play time also increased over the past quarter, too, with total logged play time increasing by four percent, year-on-year. As a result, Sony and PlayStation noted that its Game & Network Services division saw revenue grow by nine percent year-on-year, resulting in operating profit rising by 83 percent year-on-year. Notably, despite its mixed reception , Marvel's Wolverine was name-checked as a driving force for the decent performance over the past quarter - but that shouldn't be a surprise for anyone that's actually been paying attention to how the game performed . The game sold through 2.4 million copies as of 4th November (so, in roughly 50 days). Ghost of Yotei , meanwhile, has sold through 3.3 million since its launch in October 2025. More people playing consoles, and for longer - it must all be good news for Sony right? Well, not all the graphs are showing growth. PS5 hardware sales continue to gradually decline: in the reporting period, Sony sold 2.6 million PS5 consoles, down from 4 million in the same quarter in 2025. But, with 100 million PS5 units out in the wild, and 127 million PlayStation accounts across the whole ecosystem, Sony doesn't seem that worried: instead, the company is now focusing on converting those with active accounts into more viable customers. Elsewhere in the results, we heard from Sony CFO Lin Tao that the PlayStation 6 is on track and "progressing as scheduled" , with "solid progress" expected on the machine in 2027. Regarding those falling PS5 sales, Tao also referenced that, and says it's all part of the natural cycle of console launches and iteration. "Although new PS5 unit sales are gradually declining as expected at this stage of the console life cycle, the PlayStation platform continues to expand and grow in a stable manner," Tao explained. "[Next year,] we intend to make solid progress in preparing for the next-generation platform." It must be encouraging for Sony to see this growth in this quarter, especially after all the bad press and furore around the company's decision to end the manufacturing of PlayStation discs by January 2028 . It seems to be a core part of the gaming audience's understanding of game ownership, the decision has been widely contested as anti-consumer. It's caused a lot of bad blood with PlayStation players over the past six months, but - seemingly, given these results - that has translated to very little material impact on Sony's bottom line.
